Apex Trader Funding is one of the most popular prop firms for futures traders. Many traders fail the evaluation — not because the profit target is unreachable, but because the trailing drawdown and their own behavior trip them up in predictable, preventable ways.

This guide covers everything you need to know to pass the Apex Trader Funding evaluation: account sizes, profit targets, drawdown rules, consistency requirements, trading restrictions, and — most importantly — the systematic approach to daily journaling and performance tracking that separates successful traders from those who repeat the evaluation multiple times.

The Trailing Drawdown: The Most Critical Apex Rule

The most important rule in the Apex Trader Funding evaluation is the trailing drawdown — and it's also the most misunderstood. Unlike a fixed drawdown that only measures from your starting balance, the trailing drawdown follows your account equity as it grows. This means that as your account increases in value, the drawdown floor rises with it.

Example on the 50K evaluation: your trailing drawdown is $2,000, so your floor starts at $48,000. You make $1,000 and your balance peaks at $51,000 — your floor moves to $49,000. Another $1,000 takes you to $52,000 and the floor follows to $50,000. Now a bad session gives back $2,000: you are at $50,000, exactly on the floor. One dollar more in losses and the evaluation is over. On the intraday version the floor follows your highest balance during the session; on the EOD version it updates from your end-of-day balance.

The critical implication: the trailing drawdown makes it possible to fail after being clearly profitable. A trader who is up $2,000 has the same $2,000 of room as on day one, not $4,000. Where the drawdown stops trailing is different for evaluations and Performance Accounts, so check Apex's help center for your account.

Strategy recommendation: once you've grown your Apex account by 50% of the profit target, switch to half of your normal position size. Your trailing drawdown is now elevated, and the cost of a drawdown event increases dramatically. Protect the progress by reducing risk.
Apex Consistency Requirements

There is no consistency rule during the Apex evaluation. It shows up later: on Performance Accounts, Apex applies a 50% consistency rule for payouts — your largest profitable day must be under 50% of your net profit since your last approved payout. Apex raised it from 30% to 50% in March 2026; some legacy accounts may still use 30%.

In practice: if your biggest winning day on a Performance Account is $1,200, you need more than $2,400 of net profit since your last approved payout before you can request the next one. Step-by-Step Strategy to Pass the Apex Evaluation
Step 1: Define your position sizing before the evaluation starts

The most common reason traders fail the Apex evaluation is not strategy failure — it's position sizing inconsistency. Before you place your first trade, calculate your maximum risk based on the trailing drawdown. On the 50K evaluation with a $2,000 trailing drawdown, risking more than $200 per trade (10% of the drawdown) is aggressive. Define this number, write it in your trading plan in Zentrade, and do not deviate from it.
Step 2: Set a daily loss stop and a daily profit ceiling

Your daily loss stop should be a fixed dollar amount well below the trailing drawdown. A common rule of thumb is 30-40% of the drawdown: on a $2,000 trailing drawdown, stop the day at -$600 to -$800. On the EOD evaluation that also keeps you clear of the $1,000 daily loss limit. On the profit side, once you reach a Performance Account, avoid days that would push your best day toward 50% of your net profit since your last payout.
Step 3: Log every trade the day you take it

The traders who pass Apex evaluations consistently have one thing in common: they know their numbers at any point during the evaluation. They know their current equity, their trailing drawdown floor, their consistency percentage, and their daily P&L without needing to calculate it on the fly. A trading journal like Zentrade gives you this visibility in the dashboard — updated with every trade you log.
Step 4: Identify and eliminate behavioral losses

Separate your losses into two categories: strategy losses (trades that followed your plan but didn't work) and behavioral losses (trades taken outside your plan — revenge trading, FOMO entries, oversized positions). Strategy losses are acceptable and expected. Behavioral losses are the ones that fail evaluations. Use the emotional tagging system in Zentrade to track which category each losing trade belongs to. Over a week of data, the pattern becomes undeniable.
Step 5: Review your weekly report before starting each week

The Zentrade AI weekly report (Professional and ZenMode plans) lands every Monday morning with your best and worst trading hours, the emotions that show up before your losses, and specific recommendations based on your trading plan. Reviewing it before you open the platform means you start the week with a clear picture of what to fix — not just what happened.
Common Mistakes That Fail Apex Evaluations

items: Taking larger positions than your plan after a few winning days — the elevated trailing drawdown floor makes this especially dangerous
Revenge trading after a losing session and violating the daily loss stop
Trading at the end of the session to avoid closing the day negative — low-quality entries that extend losses
Not accounting for the trailing nature of the drawdown when calculating risk per trade
Trying to hit the profit target in two or three oversized days instead of building it with consistent smaller gains
Failing to document trades and not noticing patterns until after the evaluation is already over

faqItems.q: What is the Apex Trader Funding evaluation?
faqItems.a: It is a single-phase evaluation where you trade a simulated futures account and must reach a profit target ($3,000 on the 50K) without breaking the trailing drawdown ($2,000 on the 50K) or, on the EOD version, the daily loss limit. Traders who pass move on to a Performance Account.

faqItems.q: How long does the Apex Trader Funding evaluation take?
faqItems.a: Each evaluation has a 30-day time limit and no minimum number of trading days. You can pass in a few sessions, but rushing usually means oversized positions — and the trailing drawdown punishes those fast.

faqItems.q: What is the trailing drawdown in Apex Trader Funding?
faqItems.a: It is the maximum loss allowed from your highest balance. On the 50K evaluation it is $2,000: the floor starts at $48,000 and rises as your balance rises, so your room to lose stays at $2,000 even when you are profitable. Apex offers intraday and end-of-day versions.

faqItems.q: Does Apex Trader Funding have a consistency rule?
faqItems.a: Not during the evaluation. On Performance Accounts, Apex applies a 50% consistency rule for payouts: your largest profitable day must be under 50% of your net profit since your last approved payout (updated March 2026; legacy accounts may still use 30%). Zentrade calculates this for you.

faqItems.q: Can I trade NQ and ES in the Apex Trader Funding evaluation?
faqItems.a: Yes. NQ, ES, their micros (MNQ, MES), CL and GC are among the most popular contracts in Apex evaluations. Check Apex's help center for the full list of permitted products and any contract limits for your account size.

faqItems.q: What trading journal should I use for Apex Trader Funding?
faqItems.a: Use one that tracks the trailing drawdown floor and the payout consistency rule per account, not just P&L. Zentrade does both, and on the ZenMode plan it also flags revenge-trading patterns: a new trade within 30 minutes of a loss, or three or more losses in a row.
